newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Occidental begins drilling in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Occidental begins drilling in Bangladesh.

text.p: gas giant Occidental Petroleum Corp starts drilling on Monday for natural gas in Bangladesh, a country touted by experts as having huge hydrocarbon potential.
Nigel Hopkinson, chief of the company's operations in Bangladesh, said the drilling would continue for at least 60 days.
"It can go up to 90 days if we hit gas in the process," he told Reuters.

Occidental has won rights to search for hydrocarbons in the entire northeastern Sylhet region, bordering India's Meghalaya and Assam states, under a Production Sharing Contract (PSC) with the Bangladesh government. State-owned Petrobangla is already producing gas from three fields in Sylhet.
Occidental says it will spend up to $100 million in exploring three out of 23 blocs that Bangladesh has earmarked for foreign hydrocarbon firms.
The U.S. firm is currently looking for oil and natural gas in some 20 countries, and said it was eyeing gas in Bangladesh. "We are here basically for gas," said Hopkinson.
Britain's Cairn Energy Plc and two other U.S. firms -- Rexwood-Oakland International and United Meridian Corp -- have also entered into PSCs with the government for five other blocs.
More than a dozen international firms are vying for stakes in the remaining 15 blocs on offer, Energy Ministry officials said.
They said interested companies included Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Unocal , Mobil and Exxon.
Bangladesh has proven gas reserves of between 10 to 12 trillion cubic feet.
Cairn has discovered a huge offshore gas field in the Bay of Bengal. Rexwood-Oakland and United Meridian are preparing to start exploration, ministry officials said.

Petrobangla officials said United Meridian, which got a bloc in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, was awaiting a likely peace deal between the government and tribal Shanti Bahini insurgents in the area before starting operations.

Government officials said they were expecting the peace deal to be signed before the end of June. Shell abandoned exploration in the Hill Tracts in the late 1980s after insurgents abducted some of its officials. Shell, seeking to make a comeback in Bangladesh, has recently struck a joint venture exploration and production deal with Cairn and is expected to bid for four exploration blocs.
